entries.title: One row per session with what the reviewers said
entries.summary: In the Report Builder, add a scorecard question to a Sessions report and it arrives summarised for each session: Yes/No and other choices as counts (**Yes: 2 / No: 1**), scales and scores as an average, comments with the reviewer's initials. Speakers and tags can still be pivoted, so the report stays one row per session. **How to show this** switches a question to **One row per review**, and **Reviews pivot** gives one block of columns per reviewer. In SbQL: `COUNT_BY_VALUE` and `LIST_WITH_REVIEWER`, and review aggregates next to ordinary columns summarise each session.

where.path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Reviews

entries.use_case: A conference committee wants one spreadsheet row per submission with the session details, the speakers, the average score, how many reviewers called it a sales pitch and every reviewer's final comment. CS built this for AVIXA with SQL; it is now a few clicks in the Report Builder.

cs_action.note: No setup. Reports that already exist are unchanged.

internal.gotchas: Abstentions are left out of the counts and comments. On a blind Review plan comments are listed without initials. The summaries count each review once even when a session has several speakers or tags.
internal.staff_path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder (Sessions) → search a question → click it
internal.talk_track: Pick your scorecard questions by name and get one row per session, with the Yes/No counts and comments already summarised.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a review summary sheet, Yes/No tallies per submission, or comments from every reviewer next to the session details.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Plan 2.0 Review plans, especially CFP programs that hand a summary sheet to a program committee.

entries.title: Map Your Show: bring exhibitors and their booth contacts in for Advocacy
entries.summary: The **Map Your Show** app brings one show's active exhibitors into a Sessionboard event, with booths, website, description and logo, and links every booth contact with an email to their company. You can then run a Groups Advocacy campaign and **Email exhibitors** their own share links, with no portal and no spreadsheet. Syncs update only what changed in Map Your Show, keep your own edits, never create duplicates and never delete. Your Customer Success Manager connects it with the show's MYS API username, password and show code.

enable.path: Your Customer Success Manager connects the Map Your Show app for the show

where.path: Apps → Map Your Show (connected by Sessionboard)

entries.use_case: Trade show organizers whose exhibitor data lives in Map Your Show can pull every exhibitor and their contacts into Sessionboard automatically, then launch an Advocacy Groups campaign and email each contact a personal share link — without manually building the exhibitor list first.

cs_action.note: Staff-only until a real show has been connected and checked (first customer: IAAPA). Connect it with the customer's MYS API username, password and show code, then follow the first-live-run checklist in sessionboard-tam docs/integrations/mys-exhibitors.md.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a trade show or expo customer says their exhibitor list lives in Map Your Show and they want to run Advocacy for exhibitors or give exhibitors portal access without a manual import.
internal.who_should_get_it: Trade show and expo organizers — especially associations like IAAPA — who use Map Your Show as their exhibitor management system and want to run Advocacy Groups campaigns targeting exhibitor contacts.
internal.staff_path: Apps catalog → Map Your Show (staff-only gate must be lifted first)
internal.gotchas: The connector is marked staff-only in the catalog until a live show is verified — do not install it for customers yet. Response field names from the MYS API are assumed from third-party guides and not live-verified; the field mapping UI is editable if names differ. Logos are re-hosted into Sessionboard's CDN because MYS file links expire after 30 minutes. Contacts are never unlinked by a sync; categories, sponsors and contact unlinking are not in this release.
internal.talk_track: If your exhibitors are in Map Your Show, Sessionboard can pull them in automatically — accounts, contacts, booths and logos — so you can email every exhibitor contact a personal Advocacy link without building the list by hand.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should add a Map Your Show section covering: connecting the app, mapping an event, what syncs (exhibitor fields, booth assignments, logos, contacts), how the change-only write works, how to trigger a manual sync, and how to use the synced companies in an Advocacy Groups campaign.
draft.why_use_it: The App Marketplace lets you connect Sessionboard to the other platforms your event runs on, so data flows in automatically rather than through manual imports. Connecting Map Your Show keeps your exhibitor accounts and contacts current in Sessionboard, which unlocks Advocacy campaigns, portal access and CRM workflows for your exhibit hall without duplicate data entry. Field-level change tracking means a re-sync only writes what Map Your Show actually changed, so your team's edits in Sessionboard are never overwritten.

entries.title: Advocacy: native share, email a colleague, rewards milestones and per-channel analytics
entries.summary: Advocates on the Companion (magic-link, portal and admin views) now see a **Share…** button on touch devices that invokes the native share sheet (with the card image when the browser allows it) and an **Email a colleague** dialog for up to five addresses with an optional note. Every channel — intents, Instagram, WeChat, copy, download kit and QR code — now appends a `?ch=` tag to its link so clicks are attributed per channel. The **Your results** panel shows how many people the advocate's link brought, a progress bar for each milestone, the contest end date, and a public leaderboard when the organiser has enabled it. Organizers gain a **Rewards** card on the campaign page and wizard where they can add milestones (registrations or clicks) or a contest (top-N, end date, public leaderboard) with an editable unlock email; a **Who earned rewards** list with search, filter, sort and CSV export; an expanded **Top advocates** table with search, filters and export; and a new **Results by channel** table showing shares, advocates, reach, clicks, registrations and conversion — all bot- and duplicate-filtered.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign page → Rewards / Analytics / Companion

entries.use_case: An organizer running a conference can offer a free workshop seat to the first ten advocates who drive five registrations, watch which channels (LinkedIn, email, native share) are converting best in the new Results by channel table, and export the reward earners list to fulfil prizes — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The rewards card and channel table hide on a 404 until the companion API (web-api#5310) is deployed; confirm both sides are live before walking customers through rewards setup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to incentivise advocates or wants to know which social channels are driving registrations for their event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer already using Advocacy who wants to add gamification (milestones, contests) or needs channel-level attribution beyond the existing top-advocates leaderboard.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → open a campaign → Rewards card (organizer side); Companion promote page (advocate side)
internal.gotchas: Rewards card and Results by channel table require the API release (web-api#5310) to be live; they silently hide on a 404 until then. The leaderboard is only visible to advocates when the organizer has set it to public. Tagged links only apply to /r/ short links.
internal.talk_track: You can now offer prizes for top advocates — set a milestone or run a contest, and Sessionboard tracks who earned what and emails them automatically. The new Results by channel table shows you whether LinkedIn, email or native share is driving the most registrations.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/advocacy guide needs new sections covering: the Rewards card (milestones, contests, unlock email template variables), the Who earned rewards list, the Results by channel analytics table, the Email a colleague dialog, the native Share… button, and per-channel link tagging.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy turns your speakers, attendees and exhibitors into a word-of-mouth channel by giving each person a personal tracked link and a ready-made share card. Rewards and milestones give advocates a reason to keep sharing, while per-channel analytics show you exactly where registrations are coming from so you can focus your energy on what works. The Companion works on any device — including a one-tap native share sheet on phones — so advocates can spread the word in seconds from wherever they are.

entries.title: Write engagement back to plain Salesforce, with optional Timeline Tasks
entries.summary: Orgs connected to Salesforce (without Fonteva or Nimble AMS) can now use **CRM Write-back** to push engagement, activity and suggestion data to Sessionboard's custom Salesforce objects. An optional **Timeline** toggle writes one completed standard Salesforce **Task** per activity row — subject lines such as "Spoke: Session Title — Event Name" or "Attended Event Name" — so engagement appears on the Contact's activity timeline in Salesforce. Write-back also runs on a daily schedule and pushes suggestion changes immediately after a suggestion is saved or decided.

where.path: CRM → Apps → Salesforce → Write-back

entries.use_case: An association using plain Salesforce (no Fonteva or Nimble AMS) can now push speaker, reviewer and attendee engagement back to Salesforce automatically each day, and optionally surface each activity as a completed Task on the Contact's timeline — giving membership and development teams a full picture of engagement without leaving Salesforce.

cs_action.note: Plain Salesforce customers (no Fonteva/Nimble) who have the CRM add-on are now eligible for write-back. Reach out to walk them through enabling it and, if they want activity timeline entries, turning on the Timeline toggle.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Salesforce customer (without Fonteva or Nimble AMS) asks how to get engagement data back into Salesforce, or a current AMS write-back customer asks about Timeline Tasks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org on the CRM add-on with a plain Salesforce connection — associations, professional societies and event teams that use Salesforce as their system of record but do not run Fonteva or Nimble AMS.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Apps → Salesforce → Write-back; Timeline toggle is inside the write-back settings panel.
internal.gotchas: Timeline Tasks are opt-in and off by default; the toggle is only available for Salesforce connections (not HubSpot or Dataverse). Tasks are never deleted — a changed activity row is PATCHed, not removed. The daily write-back job runs at 07:00 by default (after the 06:30 people sync); nothing is written until at least one toggle is switched on. Nimble AMS WhatId on Person Accounts has not been confirmed in a live Nimble org.
internal.talk_track: If your team uses Salesforce, Sessionboard can now write every speaking engagement, attendance record, CE credit, review and award entry back to your Contacts automatically each day. You can also turn on Timeline Tasks so each activity shows up as a completed Task on the Contact record — no exports, no manual entry.

draft.docs_gap: The write-back guide should add a section covering plain Salesforce (non-AMS) setup, the Timeline toggle and its Task field mapping, the daily scheduled run, and the instant suggestion push behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Write-back keeps your Salesforce Contacts up to date with every meaningful engagement recorded in Sessionboard — sessions spoken, events attended, CE credits earned, reviews completed and award entries submitted. Because the data lands on Sessionboard's own custom objects and, optionally, as standard Tasks on the Contact timeline, your membership, development and sales teams see the full engagement picture directly in Salesforce without running manual exports. Suggestions from the AI Speaker Finder reach Salesforce within seconds of being saved or decided, so your pipeline stays current throughout the planning cycle.
problems: src/data/release-notes/2026-11-12.json [crm-writeback-plain-salesforce-timeline-tasks] article /sessionboard-crm/ams/write-back is in a self-serve suite — set "product" to that suite, or link a Platform guide

entries.title: Pick an award program or course when using CRM Nominate and Enroll actions
entries.summary: The CRM **Nominate** and **Enroll** actions — available in the Salesforce package and HubSpot card — now include searchable pickers for award programs and courses. Instead of pasting a raw ID, users can search by name and select from a filtered list: only active award programs appear for **Nominate**, and only published courses appear for **Enroll**.

where.path: CRM → People → Nominate / Enroll action (Salesforce package or HubSpot card)

entries.use_case: A membership team using the Salesforce package can now search for and select the correct award program or learning course by name when nominating or enrolling a contact, eliminating the need to look up and paste internal IDs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using the Salesforce package or HubSpot card asks how to nominate contacts for awards or enroll them in courses without manually copying IDs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the CRM add-on who use the Salesforce package or HubSpot card and run award programs or learning courses.
internal.staff_path: CRM → People → select a contact → Nominate or Enroll action in the Salesforce/HubSpot integration
internal.gotchas: The pickers are served by new API endpoints (/crm/org/:orgId/programs and /crm/org/:orgId/courses). The Public API routes and the Salesforce package picker UI ship in separate PRs (sessionboard-public-api and sessionboard-salesforce); this PR is the backend only.
internal.talk_track: Your team no longer needs to hunt down program or course IDs — they can search by name right inside Salesforce or HubSpot when nominating or enrolling a contact.

draft.docs_gap: The CRM overview guide should document the Nominate and Enroll actions, including how the award program and course pickers work and what filters apply (active programs only, published courses only).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard CRM connects your contacts to Awards and Learning so you can nominate or enroll people without leaving your existing tools. The Nominate and Enroll actions in the Salesforce package and HubSpot card let your team act on contacts in the systems they already use, keeping data in sync across your stack.

entries.title: Advocacy embeds for speakers and exhibitors/sponsors: personal share cards and "email me my link"
entries.summary: The Advocacy embed now supports **advocacy-speaking** and **advocacy-exhibiting** campaign types. Visitors to a speaker's or exhibitor's public share card see the advocate's card image (or a sample card when no render exists yet, labelled **Sample**), tracked short link, and share copy. A **Make it yours** action emails the person their own editing link. Speakers who don't have their link can request it via an "email me my link" form; the email is sent at most once every 10 minutes per speaker and the form always responds the same way regardless of whether the address matches.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Advocacy for speakers or exhibitors/sponsors; then Marketing → Advocacy

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy

entries.use_case: An event organiser running an Advocacy campaign for speakers can embed a personal share card on any webpage; speakers who misplace their link can request it by email without contacting the organiser. Exhibitor and sponsor contacts get the same self-serve experience for their company card.

cs_action.note: The advocacy-speaking and advocacy-exhibiting embed types require the campaign to be configured for those audiences; CS must set up the campaign and confirm the embed is wired to the right page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how speakers or exhibitors can share the event without logging in, or when they want to embed a personalised share card on a confirmation or portal page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using Advocacy for attendees who also want speakers, exhibitors or sponsors to amplify the event.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Speakers or Exhibitors tab
internal.gotchas: The card endpoint requires both the record UUID and a SHA-256 hash of the advocate's email — it never returns the Companion magic link. A speaker removed by an admin loses card and email access but their previously shared links keep working. The 'email me my link' form always returns 202 regardless of whether the email matches, to prevent enumeration.
internal.talk_track: Your speakers and exhibitors can now share a personalised event card from any page you embed it on, and if they lose their link they can request it themselves — no support ticket needed.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/advocacy guide should add a section covering the advocacy-speaking and advocacy-exhibiting embed types, the sample-card fallback behaviour, the "Make it yours" / "email me my link" flows, and the security model (id + email hash required, no Companion URL returned).
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets your speakers, exhibitors and sponsors promote the event through their own networks using personalised, tracked share cards and links. Each advocate gets a card that reflects their session or company, and every share is attributed so you can see who is driving registrations. The embed surfaces these cards on any page — a confirmation page, a speaker hub, or an exhibitor portal — without requiring advocates to log in to Sessionboard.

entries.title: Preview an open-link Advocacy campaign before assigning anyone
entries.summary: The **Share** console in Quick Launch now renders a live preview for open-link campaigns that have no recipients assigned yet. Optionally supply a sample attendee, exhibitor or speaker record from the event; without one, the preview uses representative made-up data (attendee Alex Rivera, exhibitor Northwind Labs, or speaker Dr. Maya Chen) so the card layout and personalisation tokens can be checked before launch. Speaker campaigns also support the **open_signup** link type used by the "I'll share a link or embed" Quick Launch option.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Quick Launch → Share console

entries.use_case: An organizer setting up an open-link Advocacy campaign can verify how the share card looks — with real or sample data — before a single advocate has been added, reducing back-and-forth after launch.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to preview an Advocacy campaign before they have imported or assigned any advocates, especially for open-link or speaker embed campaigns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy's Quick Launch with an open-link or speaker embed option.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Quick Launch → Share console (open-link campaign, zero recipients)
internal.gotchas: The sample preview uses made-up placeholder contacts when no valid event record is supplied; the source field in the payload indicates whether data is 'event' or 'made_up'. Cross-event record IDs are silently ignored and fall back to made-up data. No recipient row is created and no magic-link slug is minted during preview.
internal.talk_track: You can now open the Share console on a brand-new open-link campaign and see exactly how the card will look — with a real attendee or speaker record from your event, or with sample data — before anyone has been assigned.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining how to use the Share console preview for open-link campaigns with no recipients, including how to supply an optional sample record and what the made-up fallback data looks like.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets your speakers, attendees and exhibitors share personalised cards and links that promote your event across their own networks. Open-link campaigns give you a single shareable URL anyone can use, without needing to assign individual recipients first. The Share console shows exactly what advocates will see so you can confirm branding, copy and personalisation tokens are correct before the campaign goes live.

entries.title: Send Advocacy embed setup to your web team without requiring a Sessionboard login
entries.summary: On an Attendees campaign's **Share** tab, a new **Send setup** card lets you email the embed snippets and personal link template to up to 10 addresses (comma- or line-separated) with an optional note and a choice of registration platform. Each recipient gets a secure, login-free page at `/advocacy/setup/…` showing the **Personal card embed**, **Signup form embed**, **Open link** (when enabled), and **Personal link template**, each with a **Copy** button. The **Share** tab logs every send — address, sender, timestamp, platform, and **Opened / Not opened yet** status — and lets you **Turn off link** to revoke access at any time.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Share → Send setup

entries.use_case: When a registration vendor or web agency needs to embed the Advocacy signup form or personal card on a confirmation page, an organizer can send them a secure, no-login setup page directly from the Share tab — no copy-pasting snippets into email, no Sessionboard account required for the recipient.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their registration vendor or web team can't access the Share tab, or when embed snippets are getting mangled by email link-rewriting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an Attendees Advocacy campaign who relies on an outside vendor (registration platform, web agency) to place the embed code.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Attendees campaign] → Share → Send setup
internal.gotchas: The public setup page is token-based and login-free; tokens can be revoked from the Share tab log. The page is scrubbed from Sentry and Session Replay is disabled on it. Requires the companion API PR (same branch) to be deployed first.
internal.talk_track: You can now send your registration vendor a single link — no Sessionboard login needed — and see the moment they open it. If they leave the project, just turn off the link.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/advocacy-attendees guide should add a section explaining how to use Send setup to share embed snippets with an external web team, including how to read the send log and revoke a link.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy for attendees lets you turn every registrant into a promoter by giving them a personal share card and signup embed they can put anywhere. Sending the embed code to an outside web team or registration vendor used to require a Sessionboard login or fragile copy-paste into email. The **Send setup** card delivers a clean, login-free page with every snippet and a copy button, so your vendor can drop the embeds into a confirmation page without touching the admin console. You can see when the link is opened and revoke it the moment the work is done.

entries.title: Timed quizzes, a question bank, in-video checkpoints and answer scoring in the course builder
entries.summary: The Learning course builder gains four new authoring capabilities. **Timed quizzes** let you set a time limit on any quiz block; a countdown timer runs for learners and per-learner extra time can be granted under **Learner** settings. The **Question bank** sheet (slash command **/ Questions from the bank** or **Save to question bank** under any question) lets you search, tag-filter, add, edit, archive and restore reusable questions across courses. **In-video checkpoints** are now edited directly under the video block. Under **Learning › Approvals › Answers to score**, reviewers can award points, add notes and see a live pass/fail preview for written-answer questions.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Learning

where.path: Learning → Courses → [course] → [lesson] → Quiz block / Question block; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score

entries.use_case: Course authors who need to simulate exam conditions can add a countdown timer to any quiz and grant extra time to individual learners. The question bank lets teams build a shared library of vetted questions that can be dropped into any course, and the Answers to score queue gives reviewers a structured place to grade open-ended responses with points and notes.

cs_action.note: All capabilities are inside the self-serve Learning workspace, gated behind the Learning preview. No Platform screen changes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Learning customer asks about timed assessments, question reuse across courses, or grading written answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning workspace customers building certification or compliance courses that require timed exams or scored written responses.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Courses → [course] → lesson editor; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score
internal.gotchas: Timed quizzes and the question bank are self-serve Learning preview features; they do not appear in the Platform product. Extra time is granted per learner from the Learner panel, not from the quiz block itself.
internal.talk_track: You can now set a time limit on any quiz, save questions to a shared bank so every course author can reuse them, and grade open-ended answers with points and notes — all without leaving Sessionboard Learning.

draft.docs_gap: The existing questions-and-quizzes guide should add a section on timed quizzes and per-learner extra time; the question-bank guide should document the slash-command entry points and the archive/restore workflow; the score-written-answers guide should cover the new points, notes and live pass preview fields in the Approvals queue.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard Learning course builder lets you write, arrange and publish interactive courses without leaving your event workspace. Quizzes, branching scenarios, video checkpoints and written-answer questions are all authored in one place, so your team can build rigorous, credit-bearing learning experiences alongside your program content. The question bank keeps your best questions reusable across courses, and the scoring queue gives reviewers a clear workflow for grading open-ended responses.

entries.title: Survey feedback import: a template, required columns, and a list of rows that won't import
entries.summary: The survey file import under **Record Settings > Participant portal > Feedback** now works like Sessionboard's other imports. **Download template** gives you a spreadsheet built for the event, with **Ratings**, **Comments**, **Questions** and **Polls** sheets and a **Sessions** sheet listing every session's Session ID. The **Session ID** column matches the session code (for example SESS-12), the Sessionboard ID or your Client Session ID. The mapping step names any required column a sheet is missing and waits until you choose one. Review lists every row that won't import, with its sheet, row number and reason, and **Download list** saves it. **Download**, next to **Import**, gives you the current import to correct and upload again.

where.path: Record Settings → Participant portal → Feedback → Import

entries.use_case: An organizer importing post-session survey results can download a pre-built template that already lists every session ID, map columns with clear guidance on what is required, and get a downloadable list of any rows that failed — so they can fix and re-import without losing the rows that did match.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using the Participant Feedback beta asks how to import survey results from an external tool, or reports confusion about which columns are required during the import mapping step.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer on the Participant Feedback beta who collects session ratings outside Sessionboard and wants to display them in the speaker portal.
internal.staff_path: Record Settings → Participant portal → Feedback → Import
internal.gotchas: Feedback belongs to sessions, not people: rows match on Session ID or title, never a contact. Each import replaces the event's previous one. Download (export) answers 'nothing imported yet' when there is no import. When a Client Session ID looks like a code (another platform's SESS-21), the Client Session ID wins, and the template writes the Sessionboard ID for sessions whose code would collide.
internal.talk_track: The feedback import now works like every other import in Sessionboard: grab the template, map your columns with clear required-field labels, and get a report of any rows that didn't make it in so you can fix and retry.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Import dialog steps — template download, required-column mapping, the rows-not-imported table and CSV export, and the post-import Download button on the Feedback settings page.
draft.why_use_it: Participant Feedback lets you surface session ratings and comments directly in the speaker portal so presenters can see how their sessions were received. You control which feedback is visible, when it appears, and who can see it. Importing feedback from an external survey tool keeps all post-event data in one place without manual data entry.

entries.title: Advocacy: rewards, per-channel results, and Email a colleague sharing
entries.summary: Advocacy campaigns gain three major additions. **Rewards** let organizers set milestone thresholds (referred registrations or clicks) or run a top-N contest with an optional public leaderboard; advocates see their progress and rank in the Companion. **Per-channel analytics** break down shares, reach, clicks, registrations and conversion rate by channel (link copy, social, native share sheet, **Email a colleague**, and more). **Email a colleague** lets advocates send a personalised invite — carrying their share card and tracked link — to up to 5 addresses at a time (20 per day, one per address per campaign per 7 days). A new `{{advocacy_share_card}}` merge tag on the registration confirmation email shows the attendee's card and a **Share my card** button automatically.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign

entries.use_case: Use rewards to motivate your most active advocates with milestone prizes or a leaderboard contest, and let every attendee invite colleagues directly from their Companion — all tracked per channel so you can see exactly which sharing method drives registrations.

cs_action.note: Rewards and the colleague-invite channel are new capabilities that require organizer setup (reward rules, leaderboard visibility). Proactively walk Advocacy customers through configuring at least one milestone reward and reviewing channel analytics after launch.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Advocacy customer asks how to increase sharing volume, incentivise advocates, or understand which channels are driving registrations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an Advocacy campaign who wants to motivate advocates with prizes or needs channel-level attribution.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Rewards / Analytics → Channels
internal.gotchas: The colleague-email channel only appears when the campaign allows the 'email' channel. The confirmation share card ({{advocacy_share_card}}) only renders for registrants who are eligible to share; it is empty otherwise. Cvent, Swoogo and other external registration platforms cannot inject the merge tag — use the advocacy-attending embed or the attendee entry link instead. Only a SHA-256 hash of colleague email addresses is stored; no contact record is created.
internal.talk_track: Your advocates can now invite colleagues by email directly from their Companion, earn rewards for hitting referral milestones, and you can see exactly which sharing channel — social, email, native share — is driving registrations.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/advocacy guide needs new sections covering: (1) creating and managing rewards (milestone and contest kinds, unlock email, leaderboard settings), (2) the Email a colleague channel and its rate limits, (3) the {{advocacy_share_card}} confirmation email merge tag and its limitations with external registration platforms, and (4) the per-channel and per-advocate analytics views.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy turns your attendees, speakers and exhibitors into a word-of-mouth channel by giving each person a personalised share card and tracked link. Rewards keep advocates engaged throughout the campaign by recognising the registrations and clicks they drive. Per-channel analytics show which sharing method — social post, email, native share sheet or colleague invite — produces the most conversions, so you can focus your outreach where it works.

entries.title: Personalise your Advocacy share card with name affixes, photo framing, tone drafts, card sizes and a LinkedIn review step
entries.summary: The Advocacy share console (**Make it yours**) gains several personalisation tools for speakers and attendees sharing their card. A **Name prefix** (e.g. "Dr.") and **credentials** suffix (e.g. "MD") pre-fill from the record and repaint the card live. Photos upload natively with a drag-and-zoom **framing** step that centres on the speaker's face when the browser supports face detection. Three AI-drafted post tones — **Excited**, **Professional** and **Short** — appear alongside the event's own copy. **Download your card** now offers Square 1080×1080, **Link preview** 1200×628 and **Stories** 1080×1920 sizes. Before posting to LinkedIn, a choice dialog explains both sharing methods and a review dialog shows the final post before anything is published.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → share console (advocate's personal link or /me/promote/…)

entries.use_case: Speakers can add their title prefix and credentials to their share card, crop their headshot to look their best, pick a post tone that matches their voice, download the right card size for each channel, and review exactly what will post to LinkedIn before it goes live — all without leaving the share console.

internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Dispatch → campaign detail

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign / Dispatch detail

entries.title: Advocacy campaigns now reach every participant role, including custom roles

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Quick Launch / Links wizard / Creator console

entries.title: Advocacy tracks conversions on Sessionboard-hosted pages without a snippet

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign results

entries.title: Team campaign posts send on their scheduled date, with Pause/Resume and full Advocacy analytics
entries.summary: Dispatch team campaigns now deliver scheduled posts automatically: each post fires at its due date/time (an explicit date, a T-N days-before-event post, or a Day-N relative post), so organizers no longer need to trigger sends manually. A new **Paused** status lets you halt a campaign mid-flight and **Resume** it; a manual **Send now** while paused keeps the campaign paused. The **Advocacy Analytics** and **Activity** tabs — including KPIs, per-link rows, leaderboard, channels, geo, funnel, timeseries and the Ask "What you have here" summary — now include team campaign shares and clicks alongside community links, and each row links directly to the dispatch.

where.path: Marketing → Dispatch

entries.use_case: An event marketing team sets up a Dispatch team campaign with posts timed to go out T-7, T-3 and Day 1 of the event. Posts now fire automatically at those times without anyone clicking Send, and the team can pause the campaign if messaging needs to change mid-run. All shares and clicks from the campaign appear in Advocacy Analytics alongside community links, giving a single view of total reach.

cs_action.note: Scheduled sends run automatically via the existing schedule worker; no customer-facing setup is required. Advocacy Analytics now includes team campaign data by default.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their team campaign posts were not going out automatically, or when they want to see team campaign performance in Advocacy Analytics.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Dispatch team campaigns (marketing_dispatch / dispatches feature) who schedule posts around event dates.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Dispatch → [campaign] → Posts (to see scheduled posts and Pause/Resume); Marketing → Advocacy → Analytics (to see team campaign data)

internal.talk_track: Your team campaign posts now go out automatically on their scheduled dates — T-N before the event or a fixed date — and you can pause and resume the campaign at any time. All the shares and clicks show up in Advocacy Analytics so you see your full social reach in one place.

draft.docs_gap: The Dispatch guide should document the new Paused status, the Pause/Resume controls, how scheduled posts are claimed and sent automatically (including T-N, Day-N and fixed-date logic), the 24-hour late-post skip rule, and that team campaign data now appears in Advocacy Analytics.
draft.why_use_it: Dispatch lets you build a coordinated social-sharing campaign for your team, with pre-written posts timed around your event. Scheduled posts go out automatically at the right moment — days before the event, on the day itself, or on a fixed date — so your team's social presence stays consistent without manual intervention. You can pause a campaign at any time and resume it when ready, and every share and click from team campaigns appears in Advocacy Analytics alongside your community links for a complete picture of your event's social reach.

entries.title: Share videos, clips, audiograms and quote cards through Advocacy campaigns

Results for link-only campaigns show Shares / Clicks / Registrations — the 'Reached' tile is hidden because it would always be zero. Delete is permanent and irreversible; the confirmation dialog reminds users to pause instead if they want to keep results.
internal.talk_track: You can now launch an Advocacy campaign that never sends a single email — just grab the link or embed snippet and put it wherever your audience already is. And when a campaign has run its course, you can delete it to keep your list tidy.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the "I'll share a link or embed" who-option, the Share it yourself card (open link, QR code, embed snippet, Opens in / Open automatically controls, Preview dialog), the delete action on live campaigns, and the updated "animated card" terminology.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy campaigns let you turn speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, and attendees into active promoters of your event. Each person gets a personalised card they can share on social media, embed on their site, or send to their own network — and you track every share, click, and registration it drives. Use it when you want word-of-mouth reach beyond your own email list, or when you need a ready-made embed for a registration confirmation page.

entries.title: Generating and recompiling prints works again in Europe
entries.summary: In the EU region, generating or recompiling a print from **Program > Print** failed with "Request failed" from November 8. A queue setting pointed at the wrong region after an infrastructure move. It was corrected on November 10, and print jobs that cannot be queued now fail with an error instead of waiting forever. US and Middle East events were not affected.

where.path: Program → Print → Generate or Recompile

entries.use_case: An EU organizer preparing a printed program before an event can generate and recompile it again; anyone who saw "Request failed" between November 8 and 10 just clicks Recompile.

cs_action.note: Tell EU customers who reported print failures (SB-11358, event 183) to click Recompile; nothing else is needed.

internal.who_should_get_it: EU customers who use Print.
